decisive_semantics.reference_output_parameters: sanityCheck receives vector<int4>* loadcounts and passes the same object to JumpModel::sanityCheck; addresstable, loadpoints and partialTable are member state whose mutations survive either exception. recoverAddresses supplies member loadpoints plus a fresh cumulative loadcounts only when collectloads is true. decisive_semantics.loop_bounds_traversal_order: sanityCheck order is override return -> save original size -> at most two isReachable predecessor iterations -> single-target thunk discriminator -> model sanity -> successful truncation warning. isReachable updates parent only after a recognized constant CBRANCH whose surviving edge reaches the current parent; sizeOut!=2, non-CBRANCH and nonconstant conditions continue without updating parent. recoverAddresses order is recoverModel -> table-size check -> buildAddresses -> sanityCheck -> collapse only on collectloads success. Events expose recover>build>sanity>collapse and every early stop.
decisive_semantics.counter_accumulator_lifecycle: The original table size is captured only after the override return and is compared only after successful model sanity. The single-target absolute offset difference is compared strictly greater than 0xffff. Fixture recover/build/sanity counters start at zero; build records whether loadpoints/loadcounts pointers are present. Fresh JumpBasic production LOAD records are appended with num=1 and cumulative loadcounts are recorded after each emulated switch value; num>1 arises only after collapse or decode/clone, not at the fresh collapse producer boundary.
decisive_semantics.sorting_comparison_keys: LoadTable::operator< compares the full Address only: address-space index before offset, with no size/num tie-break. Address addition wraps through the entry's AddrSpace for both initial contiguous scan and post-sort nextaddr. The pinned GCC 16.2.1 libstdc++ std::sort uses threshold 16, introsort, heap fallback and final insertion sort; its 17-element equal-address permutation is observable because collapse subsequently compares size. Rust targets that pinned implementation, but current retained bilateral cases cover only the 16/17 threshold, not heap fallback, and the current Rust 24-case execution is absent; cross-toolchain equivalent-key order remains an explicit residual.

residuals.detail: This write-set excludes flow/funcdata, so production must consume recover_addresses_classified/try_recover_classified, preserve FailThunk separately from FailNormal, and pass the same RecoveryMode domain into truncation instead of casting into the conflicting legacy byte protocol.

branches.detail: Legacy bool/Option adapters collapse both JumpTableRecoveryError variants, unlike locked stageJumpTable's distinct catch clauses.

Locked and Rust RecoveryMode use success/normal/thunk/return/callother = 0/1/2/3/4, but flow.rs passes a direct enum cast to a legacy byte API that interprets 0/1/2/other as thunk/callother/return/default. Current FailNormal=1 therefore takes the no-return callother path instead of locked normal/default handling.

residuals.detail: LoadTable::operator< intentionally has no tie-break and the C++ standard leaves equivalent-key std::sort order unspecified. Rust targets the pinned GCC16 implementation; the current Rust 24-case projection and heap fallback remain untested, and no contract covers every supported STL/toolchain.

branches.detail: A different standard-library sort may change the later size-sensitive collapse result; portability requires pinning the production C++ oracle toolchain or defining and validating an implementation-independent contract.

residuals.detail: Rust EmulateFunction has no LoadImage callback/error channel or lastOp predecessor state: get_varnode_value falls back to zero, execute_op returns false for unsupported special operations, emulate_path returns None, and JumpBasic::build_addresses silently emits target zero. Locked Ghidra conditionally records a successfully resolved LOAD address before reading its payload, converts DataUnavailError raised during executeCurrentOp to a precise LowlevelError at that op, dispatches ordinary MULTIEQUAL from lastOp's predecessor, and preserves distinct start-MULTIEQUAL, non-MULTIEQUAL-not-in-PathMeld, BRANCH and BRANCHIND errors. Its final result-varnode read remains outside the DataUnavail catch.

branches.detail: Missing loader callback prevents byte/endianness-accurate LOAD. With collection enabled, locked executeLoad first resolves the address input, then appends its record before the payload read. Payload DataUnavail during loop executeCurrentOp is translated while that record remains visible; address-input resolution failure occurs before append.

Locked ordinary MULTIEQUAL selects the input whose incoming block matches lastOp's parent and throws `Could not execute MULTIEQUAL` if none matches; Rust neither updates lastOp on fallthrough nor performs this predecessor selection.

Locked unresolved start-MULTIEQUAL, a non-MULTIEQUAL start op absent from PathMeld, BRANCH and BRANCHIND paths retain distinct exact Lowlevel errors and fallthrough timing; Rust collapses unsupported dispatch to false/None.

For supported non-null start inputs where locked emulation throws a Lowlevel error, Rust build_addresses converts emulate_path None into address zero instead of unwinding while preserving the exact pre-error address/load/loadcount prefix.
